answer: The economy resists Sybil attacks with a stake-bonding registry: each agent enters a public atlas linking funding sources to identities, and every new identity must lock collateral in a shared lagoon. Required stake grows quadratically with the number of accounts traced to one operator. Honest agents post once and earn linearly, but an attacker minting N fake personas must post roughly N-squared stake to collect only N-fold rewards, so past a few accounts each extra identity costs more than it returns. That escalating-cost ledge makes mass impersonation self-defeating.
